ble_219_0c0581f0.name: ble_ctrl_get_sanitized_setting_20004344
ble_219_0c0581f0.summary: Return the byte at 0x20004344, forcing it to 0x0e unless it is 0x0e or 0x10
ble_219_0c0581f0.description: Reads the 8-bit global at 0x20004344. If its value is neither 0x0e nor 0x10 it is overwritten with the default 0x0e, then the (possibly corrected) value is returned. Acts as a validated getter for a two-valued configuration byte (14 or 16); the meaning (possibly a length/power/mode selector) is not evident from this function alone. Called from ble_219_0c056a50.
ble_219_0c0581f0.notes: Semantics of the 0x0e/0x10 setting not determined.

ble_219_0c05844c.name: ble_cb_slot_130dc_set
ble_219_0c05844c.summary: Store a value (likely a callback pointer) into global 0x200130dc
ble_219_0c05844c.description: Trivial setter: writes param_1 to the 32-bit global DAT_200130dc. It is called only from ble_219_0c0297b0, which also registers several other slots (0x20014600/04/08/0c/10.., 0x20015e5c), so the value is most likely a callback function pointer installed during init.

ble_219_0c0591e4.name: ble_link_get_byte_200134a4
ble_219_0c0591e4.description: Trivial getter returning the 8-bit global DAT_200134a4, located just before the 0x200134bc link/connection table. Its purpose is not clear from the code; sole caller is ble_219_0c0598b8.

ble_219_0c059390.name: ble_state_is_0x110
ble_219_0c059390.summary: Test whether the 32-bit state word at 0x200145b0 equals 0x110
ble_219_0c059390.description: Returns true when the global at 0x200145b0 (read as a 32-bit word) equals 0x110. Companion of ble_219_0c05a198 which tests the same word against 0x102. Used by ble_219_0c0572c0, ble_219_0c0573c4 and ble_219_0c05741c as a mode/variant check.
ble_219_0c059390.notes: The word looks like a configuration/chip-variant or state code; exact meaning unknown.

ble_219_0c059558.name: ble_link_table_get_base
ble_219_0c059558.summary: Return the address of the link/connection table base at 0x200134bc
ble_219_0c059558.description: Returns the constant pointer &DAT_200134bc. The structure at this address has a 0x30-byte header; the entry count byte lives at 0x200134ec and the 20-byte entries start at 0x200134ed (first byte of each entry is a lookup key, see ble_link_table_find_by_key). Called from ten functions including ble_219_0c056a50, ble_219_0c0572c0 and ble_219_0c05a91c.
ble_219_0c059558.notes: Interpretation as a connection/link table is inferred from the access pattern.

ble_219_0c0597f0.name: ble_link_table_find_by_key
ble_219_0c0597f0.summary: Find the table entry whose key byte matches and return its pointer
ble_219_0c0597f0.description: Looks up param_1 in the table at 0x200134bc: the count is the byte at 0x200134ec; if zero returns NULL. Otherwise it scans entries (stride 0x14 bytes starting at 0x200134ed) comparing the first byte of each entry (offset 0x31 from the table base) with param_1 and returns &entry (0x200134ed + 20*i) on a match, or NULL when none matches. Heavily used (callers in many modules).

params.name: param_1
params.description: key byte to search for (e.g. link/connection id)

returns.description: pointer to the matching 20-byte entry, or NULL

ble_219_0c0597f0.notes: Key is likely a link/connection handle or index.

ble_219_0c059884.name: ble_link_table_find_index_by_key
ble_219_0c059884.summary: Return the index of the table entry with the given key, or 0xff
ble_219_0c059884.description: Same linear scan as ble_link_table_find_by_key (count at 0x200134ec, 20-byte entries from 0x200134ed, key = first byte) but returns the zero-based index (masked to 8 bits) of the first matching entry, or 0xff if the table is empty or no entry matches. Only caller is ble_219_0c057d9c.

returns.description: entry index, or 0xff if not found

ble_219_0c059e9c.name: ble_state_change_notify
ble_219_0c059e9c.summary: Update the state byte at 0x20004970 and notify the registered callbacks
ble_219_0c059e9c.description: Ignores param_1 values 2 and 3 and any value equal to the current state in DAT_20004970. Otherwise stores the new state and walks the four-entry callback array at 0x20014610..0x20014620: for param_1==1 each non-NULL callback is invoked with argument 1, for param_1==0 each is invoked with argument 2. Callbacks are installed with ble_state_cb_register. No direct callers (invoked via function pointer / event).

params.name: param_1
params.description: new state: 0 or 1 (2 and 3 are ignored)

ble_219_0c059e9c.notes: Likely a BT enable/disable (or link up/down) event fan-out; exact event not confirmed.

ble_219_0c059ee8.name: ble_cb_slot_14600_set
ble_219_0c059ee8.description: Trivial setter: writes param_1 to the 32-bit global at 0x20014600. Value (likely a callback pointer) to store. Called from ble_219_0c0297b0 (a registration/init routine that also programs several sibling slots).

ble_219_0c059f00.name: ble_cb_slot_1460c_set
ble_219_0c059f00.description: Trivial setter: writes param_1 to the 32-bit global at 0x2001460c. Value (likely a callback pointer) to store. Called from ble_219_0c0297b0 (a registration/init routine that also programs several sibling slots).

ble_219_0c059f0c.name: ble_state_cb_register
ble_219_0c059f0c.summary: Install a callback into one of four notification slots at 0x20014610
ble_219_0c059f0c.description: Bounds-checks param_2 < 4 and, if valid, stores param_1 into the pointer array at 0x20014610 at index param_2; out-of-range indexes are silently ignored. The array is traversed by ble_state_change_notify. Called from ble_219_0c0297b0 during init.

ble_219_0c059f1c.name: ble_cb_slot_14608_set
ble_219_0c059f1c.summary: Store the callback pointer used by ble_event_count_reached_check
ble_219_0c059f1c.description: Writes param_1 to the 32-bit global DAT_20014608. That global is called as a function in ble_219_0c05a11c with a pointer to a small stack buffer which it fills in, so param_1 is a callback taking a pointer to an info structure. Callers: ble_219_0c02973c and ble_219_0c0297b0.

ble_219_0c059f28.name: ble_event_counters_clear
ble_219_0c059f28.summary: Zero the four counter/flag bytes at 0x20004317, 0x2000431d, 0x20004318, 0x2000431c
ble_219_0c059f28.description: Clears the four 8-bit globals DAT_20004317, DAT_2000431d, DAT_20004318 and DAT_2000431c. 0x20004317 is the running counter compared against threshold 0x20004316 in ble_event_count_reached_check; the others appear to be sibling counters/flags. No direct callers (entry point or invoked via pointer).

ble_219_0c059f5c.name: ble_ctx_get_base_20014580
ble_219_0c059f5c.summary: Return the address of the context structure at 0x20014580
ble_219_0c059f5c.description: Returns the constant pointer &DAT_20014580 (RAM structure beginning at 0x20014580; the neighbouring globals 0x20014600..0x20014620 are callback slots). Called from ble_219_0c056a50, ble_219_0c056dd0 and ble_219_0c0585a4.

ble_219_0c05a11c.name: ble_event_count_reached_check
ble_219_0c05a11c.summary: Check whether enough events have been counted and report which kind via *param_1
ble_219_0c05a11c.description: Gated by bits 0 and 3 of the flags byte at 0x200042fc (returns 0 if both clear) and by a non-zero byte at 0x20004300. If flag bit 3 is set and threshold 0x2000432f is non-zero and <= counter 0x20004330, it sets *param_1=0 and returns 1. Otherwise it calls the callback in 0x20014608 with a small stack buffer, then (only if flag bit 0 is set) requires byte 3 of that buffer to equal 4 and threshold 0x20004316 non-zero and <= counter 0x20004317, in which case *param_1=1 and it returns 1. In every other case it returns 0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: out: byte set to 0 or 1 identifying which condition was met

returns.description: 1 if a threshold has been reached, else 0

ble_219_0c05a11c.notes: Purpose of the two threshold/counter pairs (possibly link-quality or sniff/sleep event counting) is a guess.

ble_219_0c05a198.name: ble_state_is_0x102
ble_219_0c05a198.summary: Test whether the state word at 0x200145b0 equals 0x102
ble_219_0c05a198.description: Returns true when the 32-bit global at 0x200145b0 equals 0x102. Sibling of ble_state_is_0x110 and used by the same callers (ble_219_0c0572c0, ble_219_0c0573c4, ble_219_0c05741c).

ble_219_0c05a9a4.name: ble_pending_param_store
ble_219_0c05a9a4.summary: Latch a parameter pair and set a valid flag when param_1 == 2, else clear the flag
ble_219_0c05a9a4.description: If param_1 is not 2, clears the flag byte at 0x200145f8. If it is 2, stores param_2 into the 32-bit slot 0x200145f4, param_3 into byte 0x200145f9, and sets the flag at 0x200145f8 to 1. Only caller is ble_219_0c0585a4, which presumably consumes the latched values later.

params.name: param_1
params.description: event/mode selector; only the value 2 latches the data

ble_219_0c05a9c0.name: ble_hook_noop_05a9c0
ble_219_0c05a9c0.description: Single-instruction function (bx lr) with no side effects. It is called from about ten places across the controller code, so it is most likely a stubbed-out debug/trace or optional-feature hook.

ble_219_0c05a9e4.name: bt_bdaddr_reverse_inplace
ble_219_0c05a9e4.summary: Reverse the byte order of a 6-byte Bluetooth device address in place
ble_219_0c05a9e4.description: Copies the six bytes at param_1 in reverse order into a local buffer and then writes the 6 bytes back over the original (a 4-byte + 2-byte store), converting between little- and big-endian BD_ADDR representations. Equivalent to BTstack's reverse_bd_addr but operating in place. Called from ble_219_0c0581a8 and ble_219_0c05a8a0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to a 6-byte BD_ADDR, modified in place

ble_219_0c05b670.name: ble_rom_table_get_0c0810e0

ble_219_0c05b670.description: Returns the constant pointer &DAT_0c0810e0, an address inside the flash image (read-only data). Pure address accessor, used by ble_219_0c0592a4 to reach that table; its contents were not analysed here.

ble_219_0c05b71c.name: ble_rom_table_get_0c07fe00
ble_219_0c05b71c.summary: Return the address of the constant data block at 0x0c07fe00
ble_219_0c05b71c.description: Returns the constant pointer &DAT_0c07fe00 (flash read-only data). Pure address accessor used by ble_219_0c05b67c, which also uses the neighbouring pointer-table accessors at 0x0c05d48c and 0x0c05d4a4.

ble_219_0c05c2fc.name: ble_peer_bdaddr_cache_set
ble_219_0c05c2fc.summary: Cache a 6-byte address at 0x20004977 and mark it valid
ble_219_0c05c2fc.description: Copies 6 bytes from param_1 (a 4-byte word followed by a 2-byte halfword) to the unaligned RAM bytes 0x20004977..0x2000497c and sets the valid flag at 0x20004976 to 1. The data looks like a Bluetooth device address; callers ble_219_0c052ec0, ble_219_0c052f28 and ble_219_0c052fb0 are likely HCI/LL command handlers.

ble_219_0c05c920.name: ble_active_idx_set
ble_219_0c05c920.description: Writes param_1 to the 8-bit global DAT_20004992. This global is cleared to 0xff (invalid) by ble_active_idx_clear_if_match and read by ble_active_idx_get, so it holds a link/connection index or handle. No direct callers (invoked indirectly).

ble_219_0c05c92c.name: ble_active_idx_clear_if_match
ble_219_0c05c92c.summary: Reset 0x20004992 to 0xff if it equals param_1
ble_219_0c05c92c.description: Compares the byte DAT_20004992 with param_1 and, when equal, writes 0xff (the 'none' marker). Used to release the stored active index when the matching link goes away. No direct callers.

ble_219_0c05cafc.name: ble_active_idx_get
ble_219_0c05cafc.description: Trivial getter returning the stored active link index (0xff means none). No direct callers.

ble_219_0c05cb88.name: ble_counter_20012344_step
ble_219_0c05cb88.summary: Increment the counter at 0x20012344 and reset it to 0 if below 11
ble_219_0c05cb88.description: Increments the global DAT_20012344 and, if the result is less than 0xb, sets it back to 0, exactly as decompiled. The condition looks inverted for a wrap-at-11 counter, so either the decompiler mangled the comparison or the counter semantics are unusual. Called from the four similar functions ble_219_0c0540f4, 0c054180, 0c05420c and 0c054298.
ble_219_0c05cb88.notes: Condition may be a decompilation artifact (unsigned vs signed compare); verify against disassembly.
